lines.text: If your Meta ads are reaching everyone, they're converting no one. Here's exactly why.

Broad targeting means you're paying to show your ad to people who will never hire you. scripts.title: The 3-Second Hook Formula (Why Most Ads Die Immediately)
scripts.film: Screen record the Miro board at https://miro.com/app/board/BOARD_3_ID=/. Walk through each section top to bottom — pause cursor on each box, read the key point, then move on. Calm and methodical. The board is doing the visual teaching. Your voice is the commentary.

captions.text: most ads die in the first 3 seconds — not because the offer is bad, but because the hook doesn't stop anyone. the formula is simple: pattern interrupt, one piece of real value, one clear action. most businesses aren't doing any of them right.

captions.label: C
captions.text: 3 seconds to earn the next 27.

lines.text: Your ad has three seconds before someone scrolls past it forever. Here's the exact formula for making those three seconds count.

Seconds one to three — the pattern interrupt. You need to say or show something that makes their thumb stop. Not your logo. Not your company name. Something that speaks directly to a problem they're already living. A plumber who opens with 'water bill gone up lately?' stops more scrolls than 'ABC Plumbing, serving your area.' Start with them. Not you.

Seconds four to twenty — one clear piece of value. Not three tips. Not a full service rundown. One insight that makes them think: I didn't know that, or — that's exactly my problem. The moment someone learns something from your ad, you become the authority. That's when trust begins and they keep watching.

Last ten seconds — one clear next step. Not 'visit the website' and 'give us a call' and 'follow for more tips.' One action. The more options you give them, the less likely they are to do any of them. Pick the one you want and make it as easy as possible to take.
Interrupt. Deliver value. Direct to one action. That's it.

lines.text: If you're spending your entire budget on cold traffic and barely running retargeting — you're doing it backwards.

Look at this cold traffic campaign. New people, never heard of the business. Cost per lead is decent but you're working hard to get there. Meta has to show the ad multiple times before anyone converts because there's zero prior trust. These people don't know your work, haven't seen your results, have no reason to choose you over anyone else.

Now look at the retargeting campaign. Same business, same offer. But these are people who visited the website, saw a post, maybe even filled in a form and didn't book. They're warm. The trust is already there. You're not convincing anyone — you're just showing up again at the right moment and reminding them why they were interested in the first place.

Cost per lead from retargeting is almost always lower. You're paying to close, not to introduce. And the quality is higher because these people already chose to engage with your business. That's where your ad budget works the hardest — and most service businesses completely ignore it.
Cold traffic builds the funnel. Retargeting converts it. Run both.

lines.text: I see the same word in almost every service business ad, and it's costing you clicks. Let me tell you what it is and what to swap it for.
The word is 'get.' Get a free quote. Get your gutters cleaned. Get a consultation. It's everywhere, and honestly, it's lazy. It doesn't create any urgency or benefit in the person's mind.

Instead, use action words that speak to the actual outcome they want. 'Schedule your free inspection.' 'Book your plumbing fix today.' 'Protect your home from water damage.' See the difference? One shows them what happens. The other just says... get something.
When you test this swap on your ads, you're not just changing words — you're changing how people feel about clicking. They see benefit. They see movement. They click more often.
Next time you're writing ad copy, catch yourself saying 'get' and replace it with something that shows the actual value. Your click rate will thank you.

lines.text: If you run a plumbing company, HVAC business, or any service trade, you're actually sitting on a Meta ads goldmine right now. And most people don't realize it.

E-commerce is crowded as hell on Meta. You've got thousands of brands all selling the same products, all bidding against each other, all trying to stand out. The competition is insane. Service businesses? Way less noise. Plumbers, electricians, window cleaners — there's way fewer of you actually running serious ad campaigns.

But here's the bigger thing — your customer intent is already there. Someone searching for a plumber or a detailer isn't browsing. They need you now. They're ready to book or call. That warm intent means your ads convert better, which means you get better results for less.
So you've got lower competition and higher intent. That combination is powerful. Your cost per lead is lower, your quality is better, and you can scale faster than most other niches on the platform.
If you've got a real budget and serious growth goals, Meta is built for you right now.

scripts.title: One word that doubles your ad clicks
scripts.film: Film Marco sitting at a desk or casual setup, direct eye contact with camera. Natural lighting. When he mentions 'the word,' he can gesture slightly or pause for effect — keep it conversational, not theatrical.

captions.label: A
captions.text: people skip ads because they don't feel like they're for them. one word changes that.

captions.text: most ads talk at people. the best ads talk to people. it's literally one word that makes the difference. here's what to change.

lines.text: Most ads get skipped because they feel generic. But there's one word swap that makes people actually stop and click.
When you write your ad, you're probably saying things like 'get your gutters cleaned' or 'book your appointment today.' Right? Feels normal. But people scroll past it.
Now try this — swap 'your' for 'my.' Instead of 'get your gutters cleaned,' say 'get my gutters cleaned.' Suddenly it feels like someone's actually talking to them, not broadcasting at them.
We tested this with plumbers, cleaners, HVAC guys — click-through rates went up consistently. It's because people respond to specificity and directness. It feels personal instead of like an ad.
Small changes compound. That's how you scale without just throwing more money at ads.

lines.text: okay, meta versus google — which one should you actually be running for your service business? the answer might surprise you.

google ads is search. someone types in your phone number area code plus your service — plumber near me, window cleaner nearby — and boom, your ad shows up. they're actively looking. that's insanely high intent.

meta is different. someone's scrolling instagram or facebook, and your ad appears in their feed. they weren't necessarily searching for you yet. but they fit your audience. location, age, interests, maybe they've been to your website. meta builds awareness and captures intent at the same time.

real talk — google usually costs more per lead because the competition is fierce and intent is obvious. meta can cost less and get you volume, but the lead quality is different. best move? most service business owners should run both. google for the hot leads, meta to stay in front of people before they start searching.
if you've got the budget, you're not choosing between them. you're using both to own your entire funnel.

lines.text: Most service business owners waste money on cold traffic when their cheapest leads are already sitting in their pixel.

See this? This is a retargeting campaign. These are people who visited the website, looked at service pages, maybe even checked pricing. They didn't book — but they were close. They know you exist. That changes everything.

When you retarget these people, your cost per lead drops. Sometimes by half, sometimes more. Why? Because you're not starting from zero. You're not fighting cold traffic costs. You're reconnecting with someone already warm.

Most budgets get dumped into cold. But if you split your spend — some cold to keep filling the funnel, and a solid portion into retargeting — that's where conversion rates jump and cost per lead tanks.
Cold traffic builds awareness. Retargeting builds leads. One without the other leaves money on the table.

scripts.title: Why your lead cost keeps climbing

overlay.line1: Your lead cost is high because...

scripts.film: Film sitting down, casual setup, good natural light on your face. Lean in slightly on the hook. Stay still and deliberate — let your words do the work, not your hands.

captions.label: A
captions.text: most people blame the platform. the real issue is audience selection and bid strategy.

captions.label: B
captions.text: high lead cost usually means one of three things: you're bidding on the wrong audience, your landing page isn't converting, or you're not refreshing your creative. fix the audience first.

captions.label: C
captions.text: your lead cost is high because you're targeting too broad.

lines.text: Your lead cost is climbing and you think it's the platform. It's not. It's you.

Most business owners throw money at Meta, get mediocre leads, then blame the algorithm. But here's the thing — your targeting is probably way too broad. You're reaching people who aren't actually ready to buy from you right now.

The second issue is your creative isn't standing out. If you're running the same ad every month, the platform throttles you back. Your cost per result goes up because nobody's stopping to engage anymore. You need fresh creative every two to three weeks, minimum.

And third — your landing experience sucks. I mean, maybe you're sending people to your homepage or a generic form. If they can't see the value in five seconds, they're bouncing. That tells Meta your ad isn't performing, so it charges you more for the next lead.
Fix your targeting first, keep your creative fresh, and make your landing page about them — not you. That's how you actually lower your lead cost.
